chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever makes an exception in an oath, there is no breaking (of the oath) and no expiation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an oath that includes an exception clause?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni, highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) narration of Imam Ali’s (AS) legal ruling that including an exception (istithna') in an oath renders it binding without penalty for non-performance. This principle underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that 'Allah willing' or similar exceptions prevent the oath from becoming a strict vow, thereby exempting the swearer from kaffarah. It reflects the broader Islamic legal emphasis on ease and the removal of hardship in personal vows.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who makes an exclusion in an oath, so there is neither a breaking (of the oath), nor an expiation (to pay)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one makes the exception in taking an oath there is no violation or expiation.’”
